message:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001]
I’m seeking layout and design assistance for a proposal responding to an RFP. The submission would have firm requirements for file size, page numbers, and similar items. Given how RFP timelines work, the turnaround will also likely be last-minute. I suspect, though, that the RFP will be released this month. 1) Have you supported this kind of proposal before? 2) If yes, how do you plan these timelines with clients, especially when client edits may continue until the proposal is final?

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],

Yes, I frequently provide design support for RFP responses that must follow strict compliance requirements, including page limits, file size restrictions, formatting specifications, and compressed turnaround schedules. This has been the main focus of my design work for the past 15+ years.

My process is structured for tight timelines:
• As soon as the RFP is issued, I immediately build a compliant template and verify every technical requirement, including margins, fonts, file size, submission instructions, etc.
• I coordinate with your internal workplan and review schedule while allowing flexibility for edits to come in on a rolling basis
• I reserve the final 48–72 hours exclusively for redline reviews, late content additions, QA/QC, final PDF optimization, and related submission work

I’ve overseen this process many times and understand how to remain composed under pressure while delivering a polished, compliant submission by the deadline.

I’d be glad to schedule a call to talk about your specific RFP and how my qualifications could support your team.

Best regards,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

This is exactly what I was hoping to hear! Thank you, [FREELANCER_NAME_001].

Later tonight or tomorrow, I’ll follow up with some possible dates for a call.

Thanks again, and talk to you then!

At the moment, I’m available any time from 1-3pm tomorrow (Monday, 1/5). Is there any possibility you’re free within that window? The other team members I’m working with may also want to participate in the call, just so you know. Thanks!

Good morning! Great—1–3pm CST today works well for me, and anyone else from your team is welcome to join the call.

Please send over any materials you’d like me to look at beforehand.

I’ll provide the meeting scheduler through Upwork.
Good morning! I should have clarified that the time was in ET rather than CST. Could you also verify that there is no charge for the call? In the meantime, I’ll select a time. Thank you!

That time works perfectly, and there’s no fee for the call.

Speak with you soon.
Great! Thank you!
Thank you for meeting with me today. I thoroughly enjoyed our discussion and hearing more about your upcoming proposal. I believe we would collaborate well, and I’m excited to see what comes next.

Thank you, [FREELANCER_NAME_001]! Likewise. I just reviewed the current proposal, and the complete document contains 83 pages, counting all letters, forms, etc. Of those 83 pages, 55 pages include some graphic treatment. Could you share an approximate budget range for your project support? Also, would you provide one budget that includes 1 simple infographic and 1 simple map, plus a separate budget that excludes those items? Thank you!

Perfect—that information is very helpful!

For custom proposal design of this kind, I generally estimate 1 to 1.5 hours per page. This accounts for layout and visual treatment across the 55 design-focused pages, along with all meetings, revisions, on-demand assistance during the final 48 hours before submission, delivery of the complete final document, and general proposal support from start to finish.

Using that estimate, the two requested budget options are:
- Excluding the infographic and map: $3,800–$4,500
- Including 1 simple infographic and 1 simple map: $4,100–$4,800

I can work either hourly or for a fixed fee, whichever option is preferable for you. Please let me know whether these amounts are in the range you had in mind. I’m willing to make adjustments based on your feedback.
Understood! Thank you, [FREELANCER_NAME_002] review this with the rest of the team and follow up, hopefully by the end of the week.
Wonderful, have a great week!

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], I wanted to follow up regarding your message last week and check whether the team has been able to discuss this or if any questions have come up on your side.

I’m available for a brief call if that would be useful.

Thank you,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

Hi! I appreciate you following up. I recommended you to the team as my #1 choice. The lead was having difficulty viewing your profile from his side, and I’m hoping he can resolve the issue soon and confirm whether he’s interested in working with you. I’ll update you once I hear back from him. Thank you for being patient. PS The RFP still hasn’t been posted. Hopefully it will be published this month!

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], thank you very much for keeping me updated. I truly appreciate your recommendation to the team!

In case it makes access easier for him, here is my profile link:
[URL_001]

I’d also be glad to arrange a call with the team lead if he would like to ask any questions.

For scheduling purposes, I’m completely available for the remainder of January and throughout February. I’ll be away from March 4 to 16 on a family trip to celebrate my mom’s 70th birthday, so I won’t be able to actively support the project during that period.

The schedule should line up perfectly if the RFP is released this month as anticipated. I’m happy to remain flexible while everything develops.

Thanks again. I look forward to connecting soon.

Best,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

Good morning [FREELANCER_NAME_001] - TPEC, the engineering firm, would like to proceed with you. Just a heads-up that they’ll ask you to execute an NDA. After that is taken care of, I can send the prior proposal and the supporting documents so you can begin working on the layout, branding, resumes, etc. The RFP has not been released yet, so in the meantime we’re trying to prepare everything in advance. Thanks!

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],

That’s wonderful news! I have no issue signing an NDA.

Once you tell me which structure you prefer, I can create the contract in Upwork:
- Hourly: $86.00/hr, with automatic weekly billing and flexibility if the scope changes
- Fixed rate: $4,500, divided into three milestones covering contract start, first draft, and final submission for a predictable budget

*As a brief reminder from my previous message, I’ll be away from my computer March 4–16.*

Please let me know which option works best!

Thanks,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001] - Andrew Chiang from TPEC might contact you today to begin setting up the contract. He represents the engineering firm that I’m collaborating with on this proposal. I’ll remain your main proposal contact, while Andrew is essential for payment and administrative matters. I’ll share your hourly versus fixed rate choices with the firm now as well. Thanks!
Thanks for letting me know—that sounds good. I’ll watch for Andrew’s message so we can establish the Upwork contract.
One more question: can you verify that the final delivery will include the raw files, the PDF, etc.?
Absolutely. You’ll receive all original design files as well as the final PDFs.
Excellent! We also have a template from our previous submission, and maps, infographics, etc. may not be necessary. As a result, the work could require fewer hours and cost less (lower than $4500).
Once the RFP has been posted, we’ll have a clearer picture.

That’s understandable. Reusing the earlier template could eliminate the need for maps or infographics.

As part of the kickoff meeting, it would be useful to examine the previous submission together so we can determine the design direction and identify what requires updating versus what can remain as is. Without reviewing the existing materials, it’s harder for me to accurately gauge the amount of effort involved.
As soon as the contract is finalized, I intend to send you the proposal and a reference doc. I’d like you to begin the layout, branding, etc. ASAP, so I’m hoping Andrew contacts you today.
I’ll also update you on the rate structure as soon as I receive their response.
Great—I’ll remain online until 5pm EST.
[FREELANCER_NAME_001] - I’ve attached the NDA from TPEC. Thanks!
Would it be possible to provide this as a PDF?
Can you share your email address? If so, I can forward you the original version.
Alternatively, I can convert it to a PDF shortly.
Upwork policy prohibits sharing email addresses before a contract has been established. Unfortunately, the information will be flagged and removed.
No problem! I’ve now converted it to a PDF.
Please let me know whether this version works better. If it doesn’t, I can request the PDF version from the original source.
That works perfectly. I’ll review it and send it back today.
Great! Thanks.
Here is the signed version.
Thank you!!

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001]! I’m preparing a response to an RFQ that is separate from the Tpec project. It appears fairly straightforward and will involve combining all content into one document, creating the layout, org. chart, and budget sheet, and handling the formatting. The response deadline is 7/31, although I plan to submit it on 7/30. Would you be interested in assisting me with this? If yes, could you quote the total cost? I’ll also send the RFQ shortly for your reference. Thanks!
Here is the link: [URL_002]
Here’s the RFQ.⬆️
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], I really appreciate you considering me for this response. After reviewing the RFP you provided, I agree that the submission appears fairly straightforward.
Judging from the requirements, I expect the response to total approximately 20–25 pages, depending on the team. Is that consistent with your estimate?
That estimate seems reasonable. Because this is an RFQ rather than an RFP, I expect it could be somewhat shorter—perhaps no more than 20 pages.

Thank you for clarifying; that gives me a stronger understanding of the scope.

Considering the RFQ and expected page count, my project fee would be $2,400. The fee covers:
- Proposal design and creative direction
- Layout and visual treatment for the entire document
- Creation of a unified visual theme that aligns with the RFQ and client
- Incorporation of photos, graphics, tables, and any other necessary visual components
- All meetings, revisions, and ongoing support, including on-demand assistance before submission
- Final production and delivery of the complete proposal package

If this arrangement works for you, I’ll submit a proposed contract through Upwork. We can then schedule a brief kickoff call to coordinate the timeline, proposal strategy, and design direction.

Unfortunately, that exceeds my budget and seems broader in scope than I need. Could we develop a more straightforward option? I’m envisioning one formatting/layout pass on the final draft using GreenLatinos' existing brand colors and fonts, one revision round, and delivery as a print-ready PDF. More specifically, I think I need 1) layout and graphic treatment for the entire document and 2) incorporation of tables/photos/org chart/graphics into the final draft. I’m also assuming an RFP could potentially follow later, since the RFQ is typically the first step. What would this revised option cost?

I’m happy to tailor this to your needs. My fee would be $1,400 for one formatting/layout pass on the final draft using GreenLatinos' existing brand colors and fonts, along with one round of revisions.

The fee would cover:
\- Full-document layout and graphic treatment
\- Incorporating tables, photos, the org chart, and other graphics into the final draft
\- One revision round
\- Delivery of a print-ready PDF plus a Canva design link

A few important notes:
\- To stay within this budget and timeline, I’d prefer to receive all finalized content together, including the text, tables, photos, org chart, and any additional supporting materials.
\- I’ll need three business days to prepare the first draft, followed by two days for the revision.
\- I’ll build the layout in Canva, allowing you or your team to make any necessary final content changes after the revision round.

Thank you for providing the $1400.00 estimate. That works for me.

A few items:

1) My subcontractors won’t send me their content until EOD next Wednesday, so your working period will be compressed. Would you be able to turn it around within 48-hour of receiving the final narrative content from me, followed by a 24-hour turnaround on your end for the final revisions?

2) For the branding, I’ve shifted the focus from the client’s brand to the bidder’s brand—mine! I’d like the design to reflect my company, Agua Arc. I can provide my logo and colors.

3) Because this will be the first proposal I’m submitting as a prime, and I launched my company less than a year ago and work solo, I’d like to use this proposal as a template going forward. Ideally, the template you build would have modular/swappable sections so future proposals don’t need to be recreated from the beginning. In particular, I’m imagining a) a flexible narrative-section framework, since some proposals may have 5 sections v 8 sections, b) a modular table design that can be resized for different budget structures, and c) a “prepared for \_\_\_ \[client name\]” credit line instead of client branding.

4) Regarding Canva, can I own the files without having a paid subscription? Would there be any other source files, or would everything exist solely in Canva?

Thank you!
Congratulations on starting Agua Arc! It’s exciting to contribute to your first proposal as a prime.

1) That timing is workable for me. To verify the dates, I would spend Thursday the 24th and Friday the 25th preparing the first draft, with revisions taking place on Tuesday the 28th.

2) I’m glad to center the design on Agua Arc's identity rather than GreenLatinos. Please send your logo, colors, and any other materials you’d like me to use as references.

3) The modular template system you’ve outlined would be very valuable to your business over time, but it goes beyond the scope of the quoted work. Designing and testing a system that can adapt to future proposals with different section counts and budget formats requires more work than a one-time layout pass. I’d be happy to develop it, but I’d want to price that work separately so the arrangement remains fair to both of us. Would you like me to quote the modular template as an add-on now, or should we keep this initial proposal straightforward and return to the template as a separate future project?

4) I’ll only use free Canva assets, so the file won’t contain elements restricted to Pro users. After I create it, I’ll give you full editing access. You’ll own the file and can independently reuse or modify it for future proposals, including changing the client information, content, and project details.
Thank you on the congrats! :)

1) I want to clarify the timing: the other team members won’t provide their information until EOD Wed, meaning I’ll have to write the entire document on Thursday/Friday. My hope was to send you the first draft early Monday morning, 7/27, so you could work on it Monday and Tuesday. I would then review it, and you could complete the final edits on Wed or Thurs, allowing me to submit late Thursday night. Eek! The official deadline is Friday 7/31, so I could technically submit that day, although I’d prefer to send it earlier if possible. I realize the schedule is very tight, so please tell me whether you think it can work for you.
2) I’m excited that you can create the design using my Agua Arc brand! Great news. :)

3) That makes sense. For now, let’s keep this first proposal straightforward and return to the template later. Could you confirm that I’ll still be able to edit it in Canva? I want that option in case I need to make any last-minute changes after your final review.
4) It sounds like your final point answers the concern I raised in #3. 🙌 Thanks!

That schedule is workable for me. Depending on what time your content arrives Monday (7/27), I might need through early Wednesday to have the first draft ready for you. You would still have time to conduct your review and for me to make final edits ahead of a late Thursday submission.

Before then, if you can share your branding documents, I can prepare the cover page, table of contents, and overall layout while waiting for the content.

I’ll send the proposed contract for you to review.
Everything you described sounds good! I really appreciate your flexibility!
I’ll complete the contract now, then follow up by sending the branding information.
I’ve uploaded the branding-related files. Please tell me if there’s anything more you need. Thank you!
Hi! Just a quick update that I now have a document skeleton. I can send it over if receiving it early would be useful. Thanks, and enjoy your weekend!
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], the contract is fully set on our end. Thanks!
Please send the document skeleton when you’re ready; it will help me begin putting the core design structure in place.

Hi! Thank you—I’m attaching the skeleton now. Please keep two things in mind: 1) the section sequence was established by the client's Q&A, which was released Friday night, and it cannot be redesigned, so we must retain the order shown in this skeleton; and 2) the final deliverable will be one PDF submitted via email, so the template needs to support a clean PDF export that is "emailable" (I’m not sure whether I previously mentioned that). Thank you!
Great, and yes, I understand. I’ll compress the PDF so it can be sent by email.
Great! Thank you!

Hola! I realize you intend to begin once you have all the content together. Still, I’m going to add a file and note here now so I don’t forget later. I completely understand if you wait to review it until everything has arrived. I’m still aiming to send you all materials by Monday morning at the latest.
1) This folder contains photos for inclusion in the document. The images I definitely want included are marked with asterisks in their titles. [URL_003]
I’m confirming that I received it and look forward to getting the remaining materials tomorrow.
Thanks for confirming that it arrived! I’m also eager to finish everything and hand it over to you. Until then!
I’m adding one more note now so it doesn’t slip my mind later. I’ll number the comments to make them easier for you to track.
2) The proposal contains many hyperlinks, and it’s essential that all of them remain functional. I’m noting this to ensure the links still work after the final file is saved. Thank you!
3) One additional note: please ensure the fonts are uniform, using the same typefaces in the relevant sections and the correct sizes.
Good morning! Just letting you know that you’ll have the document by 9 a.m. We can discuss it more then!
Here is the document link: [URL_004]
I sent the document link to you by email and also shared it above.
The document appears lengthy, though I think much of that is due to the spacing. Hopefully, you can bring it within the page limit; please let me know if that isn’t possible.
I’m also continuing to fill in several details marked in yellow/red. I’m hoping those details will be easy for me to update in Canva.
I’m about to enter a meeting, but I’ll be available after 12 p.m. (E.T.) if any questions come up.
THANK YOU!!!!!
PS Could you please verify that you received the document and can access it?
Good morning [CLIENT_NAME_001], I’m confirming receipt and was able to open the Google docs without any issues. As I begin working through the design, I’ll reach out if I have any questions.
perfect! thanks1

Hi! One of the contractors unexpectedly sent me 4 additional resumes for the proposal. I hadn’t anticipated having more team members, so I now need to prepare 4 more bios for the Appendix under Message Agency. Could you add a placeholder for each of these 4 bios so I can insert them during my review? Thanks.
Got it—I’ll add placeholders for the bios.
Thank you!

[FREELANCER_NAME_001], I need to swap out two of the proposal’s tables, and I’m sorry for the change. The replacements are in this document. Hopefully, you haven’t reached that portion of the layout yet; if you have, I hope replacing the two tables won’t create too much inconvenience. Thank you. [URL_005]
I also added the new bios to the Tables doc, in case you’re able to insert them directly instead of using placeholders. Thank you!!

Good morning [CLIENT_NAME_001], here’s a brief progress update: I’m roughly halfway through the design, and I’ll be sure to incorporate the revised tables and bios you provided.

The document has grown to almost twice the length specified in the original scope. Because of the extra content, I’m approaching the design by keeping the proposal clear, structured, and easy to navigate without introducing excessive visual complexity.

The completed design will be somewhat more streamlined, relying on more consistent page layouts and fewer section-specific custom treatments so attention remains on the content and the proposal’s overall flow. I’ll keep working through the pages that remain and update you as the work progresses.

Good morning!

That approach works for me. Thank you.

I hadn’t expected the document to become this long, but I’m hoping we can decrease the spacing between sections and paragraphs to move it closer to the original page limit.

During my review, I’m also hoping to shorten the letter \(first page\) so it fits on one page.

If any other portions feel awkward, I can try trimming the content further when I review it, if that would help.

Thank you for collaborating with me on this and continuing to share progress updates.

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],

I’ve attached the proposal’s first draft. The Canva link is here: [URL_006]

Here are several notes for your review:

\- **General design:** Because the document became nearly twice its initial length and the timeline was short, I prioritized a cohesive design system instead of creating many distinct layouts. This should make the revisions more manageable as well.

\- **Graphics & photos:** I placed the images in organic-shaped frames and included a handful of understated graphic elements that seemed appropriate for the overall theme without distracting from the content.

\- **Section 6: Prioritization:** I didn’t find this section in the revised tables document, so I wasn’t certain whether it was still supposed to appear in the proposal.

\- **In-text bolding:** I wasn’t fully clear on which text was meant to be bold. Some content in the Google Doc was highlighted, while other text appeared in red, and during layout I couldn’t determine which formatting was deliberate and which was editorial markup.

\- **Links:** I checked every hyperlink, and they all seem to function. However, it would be helpful to have a second reviewer test each one too.

\- **Final review:** Given the very quick turnaround, I plan to make another pass tomorrow with fresh eyes to identify anything I might have overlooked. I still wanted to deliver this to you today.

I’m looking forward to your feedback. Hopefully, the draft is in a strong place, and after your review I can fine-tune whatever you’d like changed.

[FREELANCER_NAME_001] - This looks absolutely gorgeous! I LOVE IT! I particularly like the way you arranged the work samples with icons, along with how neatly everything is organized in the appendix. The small elements from my logo beneath the pictures look wonderful as well. :)

I’m going to add my comments here now so you’ll have time to consider them before making the final edits. Meanwhile, I’ll begin updating the content in the Canva version. I’ll tell you once my edits are final, which likely won’t be until tomorrow afternoon.

1) For the cover/TOC/Page Divider for Appendix and Last Page, I’m not very fond of the light pink/cream background wash on those pages. Is there another approach you could try? Otherwise, I think we should perhaps use white, consistent with the remainder of the document.

2) The letter will be one page, and I also need to insert my signature. I’m hoping I can handle that easily in Canva. However, the two pictures currently placed on the letter’s second page are two of my favorites for this proposal, so if they won’t fit in the one-page letter, I hope you can relocate them to another section.
3) On Page 15, could the tree be made more prominent in the picture? Perhaps by zooming out?
4) On Page 19, please delete the picture of the boy wearing a white t-shirt in front of the garden. You can either substitute a different photo or leave the page with only one picture.
5) For Page 24, can the picture with the lady show more of the tree?
6) On Page 30, could we also display the entire tree in this photo?
Those are all my comments for now. I’ll update you by EOD tomorrow if I have anything else to add at that point. Thanks again!

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],

I’ve completed these revisions.

1) I eliminated the cream wash, and those pages are now white to match the rest of the document
2) Letter - I responded to the comment in Canva and relocated the images to pg. 18
3) Adjusted the crop so more of the tree is visible
4) Took out the images and substituted one from the cover letter
5) Changed the crop to reveal more of the tree
5) Changed the crop to reveal more of the tree
Excellent! Thanks. I’ll tell you tomorrow if I have any further edits/comments, and I’ll keep placing comments directly in the doc as well if that’s helpful.

Good morning! I’m still making the edits directly in Canva. I wanted to alert you that I just discovered the master doc I sent you was missing a subsection from Section 2. I flagged this in the Canva comments, but I’m also providing it here so you can quickly access the content that must be added. My apologies for not catching this sooner. [URL_005]

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],

Thanks. The comments are coming through, and I’ll handle all of them at once for the v2. Please tell me when you’ve finished. I expect I’ll most likely work on it tomorrow morning.

Best,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]
Absolutely! I’m aiming to finish by EOD today, so your idea of working on it tomorrow morning works well. Thanks!

[FREELANCER_NAME_001] - Unfortunately, it became necessary to add two rows per phase to the Payment and Milestone Schedule table. I placed the updated table in the Google doc that was shared earlier today. I’m unsure whether it will be simpler for you to add two rows per phase for the new additions or replace the entire table. When you reach this revision, please let me know if you have any questions. Thanks.
Okay, everything on my side is finished! I tested every hyperlink, and they all worked!
I needed to insert some missing content that I noticed today had not transferred over earlier. I’m sorry about that.
Every one of my comments is now in the doc. Please feel free to contact me if anything is unclear. Thank you for your beautiful work and for collaborating with me under this crazy timeline.
Great, I’ll send you v2 tomorrow. If any questions come up, I’ll get in touch.
Great, thank you!!

Good morning, [CLIENT_NAME_001] -

I’ve attached GreenLatinos RFQ Response v2. The editable document remains available through the same Canva link: [URL_006]

I handled every comment where I was tagged and revised the table of contents.

I’ll be away from my computer for the next few hours, but I’ll return this evening in case you need help with any minor edits you can’t make yourself.
Excellent! Thanks for turning this around so quickly. I’ll be tied up in meetings for a while, but I’ll complete one final full read this afternoon and tell you then if I need any more support.👍

[FREELANCER_NAME_001] - I’m fitting in a little reviewing between meetings and will note anything incorrect here. 1) The tree is no longer visible enough in the photo on page 11. I’m hoping you can zoom out slightly so a bit more of the tree can be seen again. Thanks.

Hi! I’m still completing my review, with the goal of finishing by 6:30pm. I’ve made several small wording adjustments that did not affect the formatting. However, a few outsanding formatting items from yesterday still need to be fixed. They’re very minor, similar to the photo mentioned above, but I wanted to alert you. They’re identified in the Comments in the current version. Thanks, and I’ll notify you once I’m entirely finished.
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], that works. I’ve just resolved the final 3 comments and modified the image. I’ll check again after 6:30pm to determine whether anything else still needs attention.
thanks
I’ve finished! Please notify me after you’ve finalized this version by addressing any remaining issues that weren’t resolved yesterday and saving it as a final, "emailable" PDF. Thank you!
PS I’m still intending to email the doc to GL today. Thanks.
No comments remained open, so I exported the file using Canva’s digital distribution settings. Its file size is far under the standard 25mb limit.
Fantastic! I’ll test the hyperlinks in this version and then send it. I’ll follow up afterward.
Hope it’s all good!

It all worked! I’ve just emailed the submission to GL, and they acknowledged receiving it. WAHOOO! Thank you tremendously for partnering with me throughout this process. Your work is beautiful, and you demonstrated the highest level of professionalism by keeping everything on schedule—and even moving items up earlier than anticipated. I’m excited to tell TPEC how wonderful it was to work with you on this product! I’ll also remember you for any future proposals and will definitely recommend you to other colleagues. I’m planning to leave a review on Upwork as well. MIL GRACIAS DE NUEVO!!! :)
I just noticed that I hadn’t released the payment. I believe it has gone through now. Apologies for the delay, and thanks again!.

Thank you very much—it was a pleasure collaborating with you as well! Your strong organization and communication made the entire process run extremely smoothly for me.

I’m happy everything was submitted successfully, and I look forward to resuming the TPEC work later this year.

Thank you also for releasing the payment and for leaving an Upwork review; as you know, that truly makes a difference.

Enjoy your weekend, and I look forward to us working together again!
